title: Elementary
rule: Any of the 118 elements on the periodic table, including the recent synthetic ones; compounds, alloys and isotopes don't count.

traps.Water: A compound of hydrogen and oxygen, not an element.
traps.Steel: An alloy of iron and carbon.
traps.Bronze: An alloy of copper and tin.
traps.Kryptonite: A fictional mineral from Superman comics.
traps.Diamond: A form of carbon, not an element in its own right.

fact: Seaborgium, element 106, was the first element named after a person who was still alive, the chemist Glenn Seaborg.

title: Join the dots
rule: The 88 official IAU constellations count, by Latin or English name; asterisms, single stars and star clusters don't.

traps.Big Dipper: An asterism inside Ursa Major, not a constellation in its own right.
traps.Plough: An asterism inside Ursa Major, not a constellation in its own right.
traps.Pleiades: A star cluster in Taurus, not a constellation.
traps.Orion's Belt: An asterism inside Orion, not a constellation.
traps.Argo Navis: An old constellation since split into Carina, Puppis and Vela.

fact: Mensa, the Table, is the only constellation named after a feature on Earth: South Africa's Table Mountain.

title: Ninety-two
q: A Premier League or EFL club
rule: Any of the 92 clubs in the top four English divisions in 2025-26; non-league and Scottish clubs don't count.

traps.Celtic: A Scottish club, outside the English leagues.
traps.Rangers: A Scottish club; Queens Park Rangers is a different club.
traps.Carlisle United: Relegated from the EFL in 2025, so not among the 92 for 2025-26.
traps.Morecambe: Relegated from the EFL in 2025, so not among the 92 for 2025-26.

fact: Bromley were promoted to the Football League in 2024, for the first time in their history, after winning the National League play-off final at Wembley.

title: Oval Office
rule: Anyone who has held the office of US president, counted once however many terms they served; vice presidents and losing candidates don't count.

traps.Benjamin Franklin: A Founding Father who never held the presidency.
traps.Alexander Hamilton: A Founding Father and Treasury Secretary, never president.
traps.Hillary Clinton: A losing candidate in 2016, never president.
traps.Kamala Harris: A vice president and losing candidate, never president.
traps.Jefferson Davis: President of the Confederacy, not of the United States.

fact: William Henry Harrison gave the longest inaugural address on record, then died of illness 31 days into office, the shortest presidency ever.

title: Downing Street
rule: Anyone who has served as prime minister of Great Britain or the United Kingdom, counted once however many terms; opposition leaders don't count.

traps.Oliver Cromwell: Lord Protector of the Commonwealth, an office that was not prime minister.
traps.Jeremy Corbyn: Led the Labour Party but never became prime minister.
traps.Nigel Farage: Has led parties but never been prime minister.
traps.Neil Kinnock: Led the Labour Party but never became prime minister.

fact: Spencer Perceval is the only British prime minister to have been assassinated, shot in the lobby of the House of Commons in 1812.

title: Round and round
q: A moon in our solar system
rule: Named natural satellites of planets and dwarf planets count; Earth's own, artificial ones and asteroid moons don't.

traps.Moon: Earth's own satellite is excluded by the rule.
traps.Luna: Another name for Earth's satellite, which the rule excludes.
traps.Sputnik: An artificial satellite, not a natural moon.
traps.Endor: A fictional forest moon from Star Wars.
traps.Dimorphos: Orbits an asteroid, not a planet or dwarf planet.

fact: Neptune's moon Hippocamp, found in Hubble images in 2013, is only about 35 km across and may be a chunk knocked off nearby Proteus.

title: Divine intervention
q: A Greek, Roman or Norse deity
rule: Gods and goddesses of Greek, Roman or Norse myth count, including Titans and primordial deities; heroes, demigods, monsters and nymphs don't.

traps.Hercules: Usually classed as a demigod hero rather than a full god.
traps.Anubis: An Egyptian god, outside the Greek, Roman and Norse pantheons.
traps.Ra: An Egyptian sun god, outside the Greek, Roman and Norse pantheons.
traps.Medusa: A Gorgon, a monster rather than a goddess.
traps.Fenrir: A monstrous wolf of Norse myth, not a god.

fact: Fornax was the Roman goddess of ovens, and the Fornacalia festival was held in her honour so that the year's grain would be roasted without burning.

title: All the world's a stage
rule: Named characters from Shakespeare's plays; unnamed roles, actors and the poems' characters don't count.

traps.Dr Faustus: A Christopher Marlowe character, not Shakespeare's.
traps.Tamburlaine: A Christopher Marlowe character, not Shakespeare's.

fact: In The Winter's Tale, Antigonus gets Shakespeare's most famous stage direction: "Exit, pursued by a bear."

title: Brushstrokes
rule: Artists best known as painters count, including any who also sculpted; sculptors, photographers and architects don't.

Diego Velázquez: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez

traps.Auguste Rodin: A sculptor rather than a painter.
traps.Henry Moore: A sculptor rather than a painter.
traps.Donatello: A sculptor rather than a painter.
traps.Ansel Adams: A photographer rather than a painter.
traps.Antoni Gaudí: An architect rather than a painter.

fact: Carel Fabritius, a pupil of Rembrandt, died in 1654 aged 32 when a gunpowder store exploded in Delft, destroying much of his work, and only about a dozen paintings survive.

title: Maestro
rule: Composers of Western classical music, from medieval to contemporary; film, pop and jazz composers don't count.

traps.Hans Zimmer: A film composer, not a classical one.
traps.John Williams: A film composer, not a classical one.
traps.Andrew Lloyd Webber: A musical-theatre composer, not a classical one.
traps.Duke Ellington: A jazz composer, not a classical one.

fact: Carlo Gesualdo murdered his wife and her lover in 1590, yet his strange, chromatic madrigals still sound startlingly modern four centuries on.

title: Five rings
rule: Whole sports and disciplines that have awarded Olympic medals, summer or winter, current, past or confirmed for 2028; individual events and demonstration sports don't.

traps.Javelin: An athletics event rather than a sport in its own right.
traps.Marathon: An athletics event rather than a sport in its own right.
traps.Pole Vault: An athletics event rather than a sport in its own right.
traps.Netball: Has never been on the Olympic programme.
traps.Bowling: Only ever a demonstration sport, in 1988.

fact: Roque, an American variant of croquet, was played at the 1904 St Louis Games, where every competitor was American.

title: Deal me in
rule: Games played mainly with cards, including solo and trading-card games; games that use tiles, dice or a board as the main equipment don't count.

traps.Monopoly: A board game, not a card game.
traps.Chess: A board game, not a card game.
traps.Mahjong: Played with tiles rather than cards.
traps.Dominoes: Played with tiles rather than cards.
traps.Backgammon: A board game, not a card game.

fact: Cribbage is credited to the poet Sir John Suckling, said to have adapted it in the 1600s from an older game called Noddy.
